correctness.rationale: Starting from the physically stated positive two-source radial Mogi formula, a positive change of variables produces the exact derivative and the endpoint signs. The derivative ratio has logarithmic derivative with positive denominator and quadratic numerator 24x²-6(z+1)x+9z, discriminant 36(z²-22z+1), giving an exhaustive one-versus-three-root count and boundary multiplicities. At the cusp, integration of the quadratic local log-derivative yields the explicit (z-z*)^(3/2) strength-window constant. The independent executable checks symbolic identities and deterministic examples. The proof only concerns the exact idealized model.

value.rationale: The radial displacement profile is an interpretable observable for depth-separated magma-pressure sources. The exact universal 4.68556 depth-contrast cutoff excludes false inference of two radial maxima for all positive strengths below it; the explicit strength interval identifies when two annular maxima could appear above it, and the 3/2-law quantifies near-threshold fragility. This is a natural complete phase classification tied to a physical model, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a claim about generic mixtures, whose ratio test was already known. Applicability is restricted to co-located positive ideal sources.
